long_biography.plain_text:
Hsieh entered mortgage lending as a commission-based loan officer and bought the brokerage where he worked. He renamed it LoansDirect.com, developed an early internet-lending model and sold the business to E*Trade. A subsequent startup, HomeLoanCenter.com, joined IAC's LendingTree operation, giving him a second exit and deeper experience in online consumer finance.

After a non-compete period, he founded loanDepot in 2010 as a technology-led nonbank mortgage lender. The company later listed its shares publicly, while Hsieh preserved substantial voting power through founder equity. He stepped away from daily leadership for several years, returned to operating work in 2025 and is again chief executive and executive chairman. His disclosed wealth mechanism combines proceeds from earlier mortgage-company transactions with his continuing loanDepot stake. Those personal interests are distinct from the loans, servicing rights, cash, debt and technology owned by loanDepot and its subsidiaries, as well as from the company's changing stock-market value.

uncertainties.detail: This dossier concerns Anthony Li Hsieh, the Taiwan-born loanDepot founder born in 1965. It excludes Tony Hsieh, the Illinois-born Zappos executive born in 1973 who died in 2020, and other Anthony Hsieh profiles.

Forbes and loanDepot directly establish Taiwan as the birth country, so the existing United States value is corrected. The existing 3 February 1965 date is consistent with age 61 in the 2026 proxy, but the exact day and city were not independently confirmed; no city-level birthplace proposal is made.
Forbes identifies United States citizenship and Taiwan birth. Birth in Taiwan does not by itself establish current Taiwanese citizenship, so no secondary-nationality proposal is made.

The 2026 proxy discloses beneficially owned Class A and Class B shares and combined voting power. These holdings establish a continuing personal equity relationship but do not make loanDepot's mortgage assets, subsidiaries or full market capitalization Hsieh's personal property.

LoansDirect.com was sold for E*Trade shares and HomeLoanCenter.com was sold to IAC before combination with LendingTree. Transaction consideration supports a personal wealth mechanism only to the extent attributable to Hsieh's ownership; it is not carried forward as current cash wealth.

Loans originated or serviced, mortgage-servicing rights, cash, debt, technology, revenue, funded volume and stock-market value are company or market measures. They are not added to Hsieh's personal wealth; only his disclosed equity and documented sale interests are personal mechanisms.

Hsieh left the chief-executive role in 2022, returned to daily mortgage operations in 2025 and was appointed permanent chief executive in July 2025. Current 2026 company and SEC material supports founder, executive chairman, chief executive and president.

Self-made — independent start is supported by commission-based mortgage work, personally assembled funds used to acquire the first brokerage, several earlier jobs and no inherited mortgage or finance platform. His immigrant family experience supplied ordinary responsibility rather than a material transferred business asset.

The stored LinkedIn URL is an exact identity match. The existing Facebook and Bad Company Fishing Adventures Instagram accounts were retained but not duplicated; they are not used to establish the wealth mechanism. The verified Forbes and official loanDepot company site are proposed. No identity-verifiable personal X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website was established.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters and irrelevant private-family detail were excluded. Sportfishing is mentioned only in social-account verification and not treated as the principal wealth source. Current and historical vessel relationships were used only for cohort selection and were not researched or included.
